questions.sub33: What is the ratio \( \frac{r}{R} \) of the radius of the inscribed cylinder to the radius of the cone?
questions.sub34: What is the ratio \( \frac{h}{H} \) of the height of the cylinder to the height of the cone?
questions.sub35: What is the ratio \( \frac{V_{cyl}}{V_{cone}} \) of the volume of the cylinder to the volume of the cone?
questions.pic_about: A right circular cone is drawn with its apex at point A and its base lying in a horizontal plane. The center of the base is point O. The base circle of the cone has radius R; a point B on the base circle satisfies OB = R. The height of the cone is the segment AO, denoted H. Inside the cone, a right circular cylinder is placed. The cylinder shares the same base center O, so its lower base coincides with the cone's base and lies in the same horizontal plane. The cylinder's upper base is a circle with the same center O, located in a plane parallel to the base at a distance h above it; its radius is r. The lateral surface of the cone touches the upper base of the cylinder along a single circle, meaning the top edge of the cylinder is tangent to the cone's side. Point C is a point of tangency on the cone’s lateral surface directly above point B. The geometric relations are r = R·(1 − h⁄H) and the cylinder is the one of maximum volume that can be inscribed under these conditions.
